text:
alex: Quick proposal – consolidate the tenant-facing surface into a thin adapter layer that sits in front of the runtime. Goal: reduce cross-team churn when routing/auth changes happen and keep the runtime solely focused on token serving.

lin: Short version pls – are we talking new service or a library?

alex: New service (tenant-adapter) behind a feature flag. Lightweight HTTP shim with a strict contract. Responsibilities: tenant resolution, key lookup, basic auth, and routing. No model logic.

sam: How do we migrate existing callers? Many services import SessionStore directly.

alex: Migration sketch: 
1) Implement tenant-adapter with compat endpoints (/tenant/resolve, /tenant/keys, /tenant/route).
2) Add proxy mode in-session-service to forward to adapter when flag on.
3) Run canary with 10% traffic for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual opt-in per team, then flip default and deprecate old code paths.

eva: Tradeoffs: introduces one more network hop (latency), new failure domain, and operational burden. 

sam: For latency, we can do an adaptive in-process cache + async refresh. For reliability, add circuit-breaker and local fallback.

alex: Agreed. Proposed constraints in first iteration: 1) TTL cache for resolved tenant metadata (default 30s) 2) read-through mode with async refresh 3) circuit-breaker that falls back to legacy direct lookup.

lin: Ownership? Which team takes the adapter? infra or platform? Also SLOs?

alex: Proposal: infra owns runtime-critical libs, platform owns adapter (because it touches routing policies and product rules). SLOs: 99.9% 99th latency target increase budgeted to +5ms for adapter hop.

patrick: infra-bot: perf-tests queued: tenant-adapter-canary (nightly) – results will post to #eng-releases.

eva: Security: adapter needs KMS access for key material. Add audit hooks and restrict principal.

sam: How do we avoid tight coupling of adapter contract to current SessionStore shape?

alex: Keep contract minimal and versioned. Example proto endpoints (v1):
```
POST /v1/tenant/resolve { "session_id": "..." } -> { "tenant_id": "t123", "policy": "..." }
GET  /v1/tenant/keys?t=... -> { "key_id": "k1", "alg": "..." }
POST /v1/tenant/route { "tenant_id": "t123", "model": "..." } -> { "route": "runtime-a" }
```
All responses include an `x-adapter-version` header for rollout compatibility.

lin: Rollout config snippet?

alex:
```yaml
feature: tenant_adapter_v1
canary: 10%
teams: [platform, payments]
fallback: legacy_direct
cache_ttl: 30s
```

eva: Need an ops playbook: degrade gracefully to legacy path, revoke keys, and telemetry to detect regressions.

sam: Also add a static compatibility test that runs on PRs to platform libs so we don't accidentally change the contract.

alex: Good call. I'll add a compatibility CI job (contract-tests) and a perf benchmark.

patrick: infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-1429 for canary infra and CI gating.

lin: Sounds reasonable. Next steps: alex open RFC, assign owners for adapter, infra to wire up canary infra, platform to draft playbook.

alex: I'll open the RFC this afternoon: https://r/redwood/rfcs/tenant-adapter (draft). Scheduling 30m sync next Wed to walk through migration lanes. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

eva: :+1:

patrick: infra-bot: linked INFRA-1429 -> RFC  (deployment jobs will be green before canary)
